1: The presence of a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa, as seen on the upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, could also be indicative of a GIST. The contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showing a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass measuring 6×5 cm with fat attenuation in the antropyloric region further supports this possibility.
2: The patient's symptoms of epigastric pain and hematemesis, along with the presence of a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa, are consistent with a diagnosis of GIST. The biopsy showing no malignant features does not rule out GIST, as these tumors can be benign or malignant.
